Simulate a continuous time Markov chain

Source: R/ctmcProbabilistic.R
rctmc.Rd

Simulates the jumps of a continuous time Markov chain: in each state \(i\) the chain waits an exponential time with rate \(-Q_{ii}\), then jumps to \(j \ne i\) with probability \(-Q_{ij} / Q_{ii}\) (the embedded jump chain, see generatorToTransitionMatrix()).

Usage

rctmc(
  n,
  ctmc,
  initDist = numeric(),
  T = 0,
  include.T0 = TRUE,
  out.type = "list"
)

Arguments

n

Number of jumps to simulate: a positive integer, or Inf to simulate up to time T.

ctmc

A ctmc object.

initDist

Distribution of the initial state, a probability vector in the order of states(ctmc). The default, an empty vector, draws the initial state uniformly at random.

T

Time horizon: the jumps after time T are not returned. The default 0 means no horizon, which requires a finite n.

include.T0

Logical: include the initial state, at time 0, in the output?

out.type

"list" (default) or "df", the form of the output.

Value

With out.type = "list", an unnamed list of two vectors of equal length: the states visited (character) and the times at which they were entered (numeric). With out.type = "df", a data frame with the same content in the columns states and time.

Details

The simulation stops after n jumps, at the first jump after T (when T > 0), or when an absorbing state (zero exit rate) is reached, whichever comes first. The generator is used in the orientation given by the byrow slot of ctmc.

References

Anderson, D. F. (2013). Introduction to Stochastic Processes with Applications in the Biosciences. University of Wisconsin at Madison.

See also

Other continuous time Markov chains: ExpectedTime(), ctmcFit(), freq2Generator(), generatorToTransitionMatrix(), impreciseProbabilityatT(), is.CTMCirreducible(), is.TimeReversible(), probabilityatT(), transition2Generator()

Author

Sai Bhargav Yalamanchi

Examples

energyStates <- c("sigma", "sigma_star")
gen <- matrix(c(-3, 3, 1, -1), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE,
              dimnames = list(energyStates, energyStates))
molecularCTMC <- new("ctmc", states = energyStates, byrow = TRUE,
                     generator = gen, name = "Molecular Transition Model")

# all the jumps up to time 1
rctmc(n = Inf, ctmc = molecularCTMC, T = 1)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "sigma_star" "sigma"      "sigma_star"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 0.0000000 0.2886315 0.3588338
#> 
# five jumps from an initial state drawn from c(0.8, 0.2)
rctmc(n = 5, ctmc = molecularCTMC, initDist = c(0.8, 0.2),
      include.T0 = FALSE, out.type = "df")
#>       states              time
#> 1 sigma_star 0.116296115132973
#> 2      sigma 0.632502219907001
#> 3 sigma_star 0.759035449151487
#> 4      sigma  3.45244700975461
#> 5 sigma_star   3.7278060703559
